intro.data: A functor must respect composition. The source has f, g, and their composite g∘f. Map all three so the composite lands on the composite of the images.
intro.alchemy: A functor must respect composition. The source has f, g, and their composite g∘f. Map all three so the composite lands on the composite of the images.
intro.spellcraft: A functor must respect composition. The source has f, g, and their composite g∘f. Map all three so the composite lands on the composite of the images.
intro.abstract: A functor must respect composition. Map A, B, C and f, g, g∘f so F(g∘f) = F(g) ∘ F(f).

goal.data: Map all three objects and all three machines, including the composite.
goal.alchemy: Map all three materials and all three apparatuses, including the composite.
goal.spellcraft: Map all three essences and all three runes, including the composite.
goal.abstract: Map A, B, C and f, g, g∘f to their images.

afterSuccess.data: The composite mapped to the composite of the images: doing g∘f and then F, or F to each piece and then composing, give the same arrow.
afterSuccess.alchemy: The composite mapped to the composite of the images: bundling the combined process equals combining the bundled processes.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: The composite mapped to the composite of the images: setting the combined working equals combining the set workings.
afterSuccess.abstract: The composite mapped to the composite of the images: F(g∘f) = F(g) ∘ F(f).

reveal.summary: Functors preserve composition: F(g ∘ f) = F(g) ∘ F(f). The image of a combined step is the combination of the imaged steps.
reveal.moreFormal: Together with F(id_A) = id_F(A), this is the full definition of a functor: it preserves identities and composition, so it carries every commuting diagram in C to a commuting diagram in D.
